strongest_angle: The comparison between Sherlock Holmes and Count Dracula represents a collision between Victorian rationalism and supernatural gothic horror, as explored in both academic analysis and literary pastiches.

key_facts.fact: Loren D. Estleman published the novel Sherlock Holmes vs. Dracula, or the Adventure of the Sanguinary Count in 1978, which depicts a direct encounter between the two characters.
In the first Sherlock Holmes story, Arthur Conan Doyle writes that Watson compares Holmes's deductive powers to supernatural abilities, stating he would have been burned centuries ago.
key_facts.source_name: Sherlock the Vampire…or the Vampire Hunter? – Late 19th Century British Literature & Culture

key_facts.fact: Academic analysis by Daniel Cottom identifies Sherlock Holmes as the fantastic end of the bohemian figure, while Count Dracula represents its fantasized origin in late 19th-century culture.

quotes.text: Mr. Sherlock Holmes? His voice was as deep and devoid of emotion as the bass note of an organ in a cathedral. The detective nodded. I am Count Dracula.
quotes.speaker: Count Dracula

quotes.text: You would certainly have been burned, had you lived a few centuries ago, Watson declares
quotes.speaker: John Watson
